newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - European shares mixed, dollar gains ground.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - European shares mixed, dollar gains ground.

text.p: European shares gave a muted reaction to an overnight fall on Wall Street in early trading on Wednesday while the dollar gained a little ground against both the mark and the yen.
The Frankfurt and Paris bourses made moderate gains in mid-morning business but London, Europe's busiest stock market, was back in the minus column after fluctuating up and down.

Markets generally were focusing on key U.S. February consumer price data due at 1330 GMT for clues on likely action at next week's meeting of the policy-making committee of the U.S. central bank, the Federal Reserve.
Concern about higher interest rates to keep a lid on inflation depressed U.S. shares on Tuesday. Traders noted a growing belief in world markets that U.S. rates will rise on March 25.
"Inflation data in the U.S. has been consistently benign," one share dealer said. "But that won't stop the Fed raising rates pre-emptively because the economy is very strong."
London shares opened lower after news that Wall Street ended almost 59 points or 0.85 percent weaker -- more than double the 25-point loss it showed as London closed for business on Tuesday.

They then moved ahead, aided by firmer bonds and a strong performance by British Telecom shares (up 12 pence at 454), before slipping back again as strong British data hit bond prices amid concern about higher interest rates.
German shares advanced after February money supply data and a key business confidence survey were viewed as mildly positive signs for the economy.

M3 money growth slowed to a 9.1 percent annualised rate from the fourth 1996 quarter from January's 11.7 percent rise. The Ifo institute February German business climate index rose to 93.6 from 93.3 in January.

Steel giants Thyssen and Krupp have agreed to talk on setting up a joint steel company, the state government of North Rhine-Westphalia said a day after Krupp launched a hostile bid for its bigger rival. Their shares were still suspended.
The Paris bourse, shrugging off Wall Street's dip, was also boosted at the opening by higher bond prices and a stronger dollar, good news for exporters.
"Paris has in the past few days fallen much more than Wall Street," one dealer said.
On the currency market, the dollar edged higher, moving above 1.68 marks and 123 yen in cautious trading before slipping from its highs.
But the mark, already boosted as a "safe haven" by market concerns over the timing of European monetary union, edged up against other continental European currencies.

The pound, hit by jitters this week after confirmation that a general election will take place on May 1, edged up after news that the British February jobless rate fell to 6.2 percent from 6.5 in January.
Sterling gained to 2.6790 marks, after a session peak of 2.6820 marks, compared with 2.6607 overnight, and to $1.5929 from $1.5887.
CURRENCIES AT 1015 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.6820 marks and 123 yen, compared with Tuesday's late European levels of 1.6762 and 122.44.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1015 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 11.0 points at 4,345.8.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 10.19 points at 2,584.14.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was 12.40 ahead at 3,303.59.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $348.95 in the morning, up from the previous London close of $346.25. Silver rose to $5.18 from $5.10.
